segments.text: Soldiers who come back from a battle site may find
that the battle does not end when they return to society
Substance abuse, suicide, family collapse due to PTSD
Even if one survives the war, lives can still be lost in the years that follow
My friend Michael was a US soldier who fought in Iraq
After returning home he would panic or become angry than at small sounds
The sound of fireworks, the slam of a car door
These reminded him of the explosions of the battlefield
Michael also could not sleep and suffered from nightmares
His wife tried to support him
But life with him, as he grew aggressive, was hard
Michael then came to rely on drugs
A veteran support organization
Reached out to him
Counseling group therapy
Dialogue with comrades
My God, slowly recovered, now he does work to support other veterans
War may break you, but it does not have to define you
Politicians start wars, but it is the young who fight
Care after return is the responsibility of the nation that sent them to war
It is not only soldiers who suffer PTSD, victims of abuse
Though struck by disaster, because wounds of the heart are invisible
So they remain long
For society to turn its eyes
To the wounds of the heart
And build a system of support
That is the condition
Of a kind society
you
